You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Generate beautiful landing pages for your projects.

Description

oranda is a static-site generator intended for publishing project landing pages and documentation. It focuses on making it simple to create a professional project website with minimal configuration.

Quickstart

# build your site

> oranda dev

Configuration

oranda

Generate beautiful landing pages for your projects.

Description

oranda is a static-site generator intended for publishing project landing pages and documentation. It focuses on making it simple to create a professional project website with minimal configuration.

Quickstart

# build your site
> oranda build

# build your site and start a server that rebuilds on file changes
> oranda dev

Configuration

oranda is designed to work without a configuration file for many projects. If you wish to customize behavior, place an oranda.json file in your project's root and consult the published documentation for configuration options.

More information

See the project's published documentation and website for additional usage examples and guides.

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, builder::{PossibleValuesParser, PossibleValue}};
use std::process::ExitCode;

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    let verbose = Arg::new("verbose")
        .short('v')
        .long("verbose")
        .help("Whether to output more detailed debug information")
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
        .global(true);
    let output_format = Arg::new("output-format")
        .long("output-format")
        .value_name("OUTPUT_FORMAT")
        .help("The format of the output")
        .default_value("human")
        .value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new([
            PossibleValue::new("human").help("Human-readable output"),
            PossibleValue::new("json").help("Machine-readable JSON output"),
        ]))
        .global(true);

    let build_cmd = Command::new("build")
        .about("Build an oranda site")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("json-only")
                .long("json-only")
                .help("Only build the artifacts JSON file (if applicable) and other files that may be used to support it, such as installer source files")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        );

    let dev_cmd = Command::new("dev")
        .about("Start a local development server that recompiles your oranda site if a file changes")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("port")
                .long("port")
                .value_name("PORT")
                .help("The port for the file server to be launched on")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u16)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no-first-build")
                .long("no-first-build")
                .help("Skip the first build before starting to watch for changes")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("include-paths")
                .short('i')
                .long("include-paths")
                .value_name("INCLUDE_PATHS")
                .help("List of extra paths to watch")
                .action(ArgAction::Append),
        );

    let serve_cmd = Command::new("serve")
        .about("Start a file server to access your oranda site in a browser")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("port")
                .long("port")
                .value_name("PORT")
                .default_value("7979")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u16)),
        );

    let output_path_arg = || {
        Arg::new("output-path")
            .short('o')
            .long("output-path")
            .value_name("OUTPUT_PATH")
            .help("Path to the output file")
    };
    let site_path_arg = || {
        Arg::new("site-path")
            .short('s')
            .long("site-path")
            .value_name("SITE_PATH")
            .help("Path to your oranda site")
    };

    let ci_cmd = Command::new("ci")
        .about("Generates a CI file that can be used to deploy your site")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("ci")
                .long("ci")
                .value_name("CI")
                .help("What CI to generate a file for")
                .default_value("github")
                .value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new([
                    PossibleValue::new("github").help("Deploy to GitHub Pages using GitHub Actions"),
                ])),
        )
        .arg(output_path_arg())
        .arg(site_path_arg());

    let generate_cmd = Command::new("generate")
        .about("Generate infrastructure files for oranda sites")
        .arg(output_path_arg())
        .arg(site_path_arg())
        .subcommand(ci_cmd);

    Command::new("oranda")
        .version("0.6.5")
        .about("🎁 generate beautiful landing pages for your projects")
        .arg(verbose)
        .arg(output_format)
        .subcommand(build_cmd)
        .subcommand(dev_cmd)
        .subcommand(serve_cmd)
        .subcommand(generate_cmd)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let m = build_cli().get_matches();
    // stub: just print something
    println!("matched");
    ExitCode::from(0)
}

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, builder::{PossibleValuesParser, PossibleValue}};
use std::process::ExitCode;

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    let verbose = Arg::new("verbose")
        .short('v')
        .long("verbose")
        .help("Whether to output more detailed debug information").help_heading("GLOBAL OPTIONS")
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
        .global(true);
    let output_format = Arg::new("output-format")
        .long("output-format")
        .value_name("OUTPUT_FORMAT")
        .help("The format of the output").help_heading("GLOBAL OPTIONS")
        .default_value("human")
        .value_parser(PossibleValuesParser::new([
            PossibleValue::new("human").help("Human-readable output"),
            PossibleValue::new("json").help("Machine-readable JSON output"),
        ]))
        .global(true);

    let build_cmd = Command::new("build")
        .about("Build an oranda site")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("json-only")
                .long("json-only")
                .help("Only build the artifacts JSON file (if applicable) and other files that may be used to support it, such as installer source files")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        );

    let dev_cmd = Command::new("dev")
        .about("Start a local development server that recompiles your oranda site if a file changes")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("port")
                .long("port")
                .value_name("PORT")
                .help("The port for the file server to be launched on")
                .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u16)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no-first-build")
                .long("no-first-build")
                .help("Skip the first build before starting to watch for changes")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("include-paths")
                .short('i')
                .long("include-paths")
                .value_name("INCLUDE_PATHS")
</output>

// Wrap text at given width, breaking at spaces
fn wrap_cause(text: &str, width: usize, first_prefix: &str, cont_prefix: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    // width is max text width per line (excluding prefix? we handle)
    // Actually we want max total? Let's use text width 112
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    let mut remaining = text;
    let mut first = true;
    while remaining.len() > width {
        // Find last space before width
        let slice = &remaining[..width.min(remaining.len())];
        // Need to handle byte vs char: cause is ascii (no multibyte except backticks? backticks ascii). So byte index == char.
        // Find last space
        if let Some(idx) = slice.rfind(' ') {
            let (head, tail) = remaining.split_at(idx);
            lines.push(if first { format!("{}{}", first_prefix, head) } else { format!("{}{}", cont_prefix, head) });
            remaining = tail.trim_start();
            first = false;
        } else {
            // No space, break at width
            let (head, tail) = remaining.split_at(width);
            lines.push(if first { format!("{}{}", first_prefix, head) } else { format!("{}{}", cont_prefix, head) });
            remaining = tail;
            first = false;
        }
        // For continuation, prefix changes? Already handled. For next iteration, use cont_prefix
        // Actually after first, all use cont_prefix. So update prefixes?
        // We'll just keep using cont_prefix after first
    }
    lines.push(if first { format!("{}{}", first_prefix, remaining) } else { format!("{}{}", cont_prefix, remaining) });
    lines
}

fn json_escape(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len()+2);
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32)),
            _ => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}
